-monotonic way: it rises early and then flattens or falls back, depending on P. A purely additive f(P)+g(t) model leaves NMSE near 2e-2, so P and t interact.

I ran out of tool calls before finding the time-dependence. The submitted candidate is not a good answer; the best fit was about 0.0026 NMSE.

import numpy as np
def equation(t, P, params):
    g = 1 + params[4]*t*np.exp(-params[5]*t) + params[6]*np.sin(params[7]*t+params[8])
    return (params[0] + params[1]*P + params[2]*P**2 + params[3]*P**3) * g
